newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore, Egypt to sign first trade memorandum.
newsitem.headline: Singapore, Egypt to sign first trade memorandum.

text.p: Singapore said on Wednesday it will sign a memorandum of understanding (MOU) to promote trade with Egypt, the first ever to be signed between the two countries, a government statement said.
The MOU, to be signed on Thursday, will stimulate the exchange of timely economic and business information, it said.
The signing coincides with Egyptian Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri's three-day visit to Singapore to boost trade and other ties. He leaves on Thursday for Beijing.
Singapore's Trade and Development Board (TDB) Deputy Chairman Kwek Leng Joo and Egypt's Ambassador and Assistant Minister of Foreign Affairs Sayed Abou Zaid will sign the MOU.
"Despite our long history of trading ties, the Egyptian market is still relatively unknown to Singapore businessmen," Kwek said in the government's statement.
On Tuesday, the two countries signed an investment guarantee agreement to give investors more confidence and protection in the business projects of both countries.
They have also agreed to share in organising trade exhibitions and seminars on products and services and in developing and promoting trade expansion.

The TDB will conduct a mission to Egypt in the third quarter of this year and another in 1998. The Port of Singapore Authority is set to send a delegation to Egypt to exchange ideas on trade and shipping.
Singapore's bilateral trade with Egypt has been increasing at an average annual rate of 11 percent since 1988.
Bilateral trade between the two totalled S$332.7 million (US$231 million) in 1996, a 13.8 percent decline over 1995's S$386 million.
